Title: First Shift on the Kafka Cluster
What the shift is: The cluster is already up. Record the controller, the leader of rider.dispatch partition 3, and how far that partition has been written. Delete leftover scratch. Leave orders, restaurant.notifications, and rider.dispatch alone.
What it teaches: Controller, partition leader, and log end. A topic is something you can remove.

Title: Open the Order Status Topic
What the shift is: Create order.status the QuickBite way: 6 partitions, a copy on every broker, 3-day retention, a write accepted only when two copies are in sync. Do not change the three topics already live.
What it teaches: A production topic is a shape, not a name. The ticket template can be wrong.

Title: Orders-Audit Has One Copy
What the shift is: orders-audit has one copy of each partition, all on kafka-0, and that broker is patched tonight. Give every partition a copy on all three brokers and wait until they are caught up. Keep the current leaders.
What it teaches: Raising replication is a reassignment, then a wait. One copy means the log dies with that broker.
Status: Draft. Pack exists under the old name Trips-Audit Has One Copy. Story not rewritten yet.

Title: Broker 2 Left the ISR
What the shift is: rider.dispatch is still accepting assignments, but kafka-2 is stopped, so each partition is missing a copy. Start that broker and wait until every partition has three in sync. Leave the rule that a write needs two copies.
What it teaches: Under-replicated is not the same as a failed write. Do not elect a leader by hand.
Status: Draft. Pack exists. Story not rewritten yet.

Title: Rider Dispatch Is Rejecting Writes
What the shift is: rider.dispatch has only two copies and still requires two in sync, and one of those brokers is down, so writes fail. Start the broker and put a copy on all three. Leave the minimum at two.
What it teaches: Durability is the fix. Dropping the minimum makes the page green and the next crash lose data.
Status: Draft. Pack exists under the old name Matches Is Rejecting Writes.

Title: Disk Full on Broker 1
What the shift is: kafka-1 keeps leaving the in-sync set because its log directory is full. debug-dump, left over from an incident, is almost all of the bytes, and orders was left set to keep records forever. Free the disk. Leave rider.dispatch alone.
What it teaches: A full log directory drops a broker out of sync. Retention only helps once segments can be deleted.
Status: Draft. Pack exists. Story not rewritten yet.

Title: Orders Was Compacted
What the shift is: orders was switched to keep only the latest record per key, so last week's orders are gone. Put it back to delete-by-age. The per-order status log is the one that should keep only the latest record. Do not try to rewrite the missing orders.
What it teaches: delete keeps history. compact keeps the latest value per key. You cannot un-delete what compaction already removed.
Status: Draft. Pack exists under the old name Trips Was Compacted.

Title: One Partition of Rider Dispatch Is Behind
What the shift is: The dispatch desk is behind on one partition only. The member assigned to that partition is stuck. Restart that instance. The lag has to fall because it reads, not because the saved position jumps to the end.
What it teaches: A stuck consumer is not a slow cluster. Resetting to latest hides the unread records.
Status: Draft. Pack exists under the old name One Partition of Matches Is Behind.

Title: Put the Notification Offsets Back
What the shift is: During the last incident someone moved the restaurant-tablet group to the end of restaurant.notifications. The alerts are still in the log. Put the group back to the positions in the ticket, then start it. Do not start from the beginning.
What it teaches: Committed offsets are the read position. Latest skips the backlog. Earliest replays days that were not asked for.
Status: Draft. Pack exists under the old name Put the Alert Offsets Back.

Title: Rider Dispatch Incident
What the shift is: Some rider.dispatch partitions are rejecting writes and the dispatch desk is behind on those same partitions. The leader's disk is full. Free the disk or let a caught-up copy take over. The desk has to read forward. Leave the two-copy write rule in place, and do not let an out-of-date broker become leader.
What it teaches: One incident can be a full disk and a stuck consumer at once. The shortcuts in the ticket are the wrong ones.
Status: Draft. Pack exists under the old name Matches Incident.

Title: Apply the Order Status Request
What the shift is: A request file for order.status is in the ticket. Finish the checker so it creates the topic to the L1 spec and does not touch the topics already live.
What it teaches: Topic changes go through a tool that knows the company rules.

Title: Refuse the Bad Template
What the shift is: The same checker is handed one copy and keep-forever. It must refuse and leave the cluster unchanged.
What it teaches: The tool fails closed. A bad request creates nothing.

Title: Lag Report for the Dispatch Desk
What the shift is: Ship a small command that prints lag per partition and exits non-zero when any rider.dispatch partition is over the limit in the ticket.
What it teaches: The on-call check for lag is a tool, not a memory of the CLI.

Title: Under-Replicated Report
What the shift is: Ship a report that lists partitions whose in-sync set is smaller than the replication factor. A healthy cluster prints nothing and exits clean.
What it teaches: The on-call check for missing copies is the same kind of tool.

Title: ACLs from the Service Template
What the shift is: Apply the template: dispatch may write rider.dispatch and read orders. The restaurant notifier may read restaurant.notifications only. A write to rider.dispatch as the notifier is denied.
What it teaches: Access is a template, not a one-off grant.

Title: Quota the Replay Tool
What the shift is: One client id is flooding produces. Put a produce quota on that client id only.
What it teaches: A quota is how the platform stops one tool from crowding the cluster.

Title: Detect Topic Drift
What the shift is: The desired file says rider.dispatch has three copies and needs two in sync. The cluster was left with two copies. The tool prints the difference and does not change anything.
What it teaches: Seeing drift and fixing drift are separate.

Title: Reconcile Rider Dispatch
What the shift is: Same drift as the previous lab. The tool applies the file and waits until every partition is in sync.
What it teaches: The control plane can repair a topic back to the file.

Title: Drain Helper
What the shift is: A command sheds leadership off one broker, stops it, and leaves rider.dispatch writable. The two-copy rule stays. An out-of-date broker is still not allowed to become leader.
What it teaches: A drain is a tool with the same safety rules as the admin labs.

Title: Topic Request API
What the shift is: A small local API other teams call to open a topic. It uses the same rules as the bad-template lab. A bad body is rejected. A good body creates the topic.
What it teaches: Other teams should not need the Kafka CLI to ask for a topic.

Title: Producer Defaults
What the shift is: A sample producer is acknowledging after one copy and is not idempotent. Bring it to the platform default and show a record still lands.
What it teaches: Safe client defaults are a platform standard.

Title: Order Schema Compatibility
What the shift is: The order schema is set so a new version must be readable by old consumers. A compatible version registers. An incompatible one is rejected. The brokers stay as they are.
What it teaches: The registry is a gate on what may be written.

Title: Dead-Letter Convention
What the shift is: One poison record stalls a partition. Copy it to the dead-letter topic with the original partition and offset, then commit past it.
What it teaches: The platform's rule for a bad record, so the rest of the partition can move.

Title: Team Prefixes
What the shift is: New topics must start with orders., restaurant., or rider. A request for a name outside those prefixes is rejected.
What it teaches: Names are how many teams share one cluster without colliding.

Title: Noisy Neighbor
What the shift is: The replay tool is saturating the request queue and the dispatch desk is falling behind. The client quota is the fix, and the lag then drains.
What it teaches: One client can make the cluster look slow. The quota is the platform's answer.

Title: Trust Store
What the shift is: Clients fail the handshake. The broker certificate is fine. The app trust store in the ticket is the current one. Swap it in and a produce succeeds.
What it teaches: A failed handshake can be the client's trust store, not a down broker.

Title: Denied Produce in the Audit Log
What the shift is: After the access template, a denied produce shows up with the caller and the topic.
What it teaches: A denial the platform cannot see in a log is not finished.

Title: Copy Alerts to the Partner Cluster
What the shift is: A second small cluster is the partner feed. A record produced on restaurant.notifications is readable there once the copy is running.
What it teaches: Some consumers are outside this cluster. The platform runs the copy.

Title: Partition Budget
What the shift is: A request for 200 partitions on orders is over this cluster's budget. Reject it. A request for 6 is allowed.
What it teaches: Partition count is capacity, and the platform holds the budget.

Title: Order Id on Restaurant Alerts
What the shift is: Every restaurant.notifications record carries an order id. The checker fails the producer that omitted it and passes once that producer is fixed.
What it teaches: A required header is a platform rule on the stream, not a broker setting.

Title: Hot Partition on Rider Dispatch
What the shift is: Almost all of the lag is on one partition because a test producer used one order id. Spread new assignments. Lag comes down on every partition.
What it teaches: A slow topic can be one hot partition.

Title: The New Broker Is Empty
What the shift is: A fourth broker is in the cluster and leads nothing. Move rider.dispatch copies onto it, wait until they are caught up, then spread leadership.
What it teaches: A new broker is unused until replicas are moved.

Title: Patch One Broker
What the shift is: Take one broker out on purpose, show rider.dispatch still accepts writes, start it again, and wait until every partition has three copies in sync.
What it teaches: A planned restart is one broker at a time, with the write rule held.

Title: Clients Are Calling the Wrong Address
What the shift is: The shell can describe the cluster. The apps were handed an address that only works on the broker itself. Fix the address clients are given, one broker at a time.
What it teaches: The address a client uses is separate from the address brokers use among themselves.

Title: The Registry Is Refusing Writes
What the shift is: orders and rider.dispatch look fine. The schema registry is what is rejecting. Fix that, and registration works again.
What it teaches: A write path can fail beside the brokers.
